---
title: "Authentication"
---

Some package repositories need a username and a password, or a token: a
private Posit Package Manager (PPM) instance, or your company's
Artifactory or Nexus server. rig sends HTTP basic authentication to these
whenever it downloads from them, including downloading package metadata and
packages in [`rig pkg`](reference/pkg.qmd) and
[`rig proj`](reference/proj.qmd).

rig works the same way as [pak](https://pak.r-lib.org/reference/repo-auth.html),
and uses the same netrc file, credential store keys and PPM token file. So if
your credentials work with pak, they work with rig as well, and the other way
around.

::: {.callout-note}
These credentials are only used by rig itself. If you call
`install.packages()` from R, R downloads the packages, and it does not use
them. Use pak from R, or give R the credentials some other way.
:::

## Usernames in repository URLs

To tell rig which username to use for a repository, put it into the URL of
the repository:

```sh
rig repos add acme https://alice@cran.acme.com/cran --enable
```

The username is part of the URL everywhere rig stores it: in the rig
configuration file, in `rproj.toml`, in `rproj.lock`, and in the
`repositories` file of the R installation. A password never is. rig refuses
to add a repository URL with a password in it, with `rig repos add` or in
`rproj.toml`.

You do not always need a username. A PPM SSO token, a netrc file and the
environment variables below also work for URLs without one.

## Where rig looks for credentials

For every URL, rig looks for credentials in this order, and uses the first
it finds:

1. **A password in the URL.** You can only do this for URLs on the command
   line, with `--with-repos`, e.g.
   `rig pkg install --with-repos acme=https://alice:secret@cran.acme.com/cran pkg`.
   rig removes the password from the URL and keeps it in memory only, it
   does not write it to any file.
2. **Environment variables.** `RIG_REPO_<NAME>_USERNAME` and
   `RIG_REPO_<NAME>_PASSWORD`, for the repository named `<NAME>`. The name
   is in upper case, and every character that is not a letter or a digit is
   replaced by `_`. E.g. for a repository called `acme-cran`:

   ```sh
   export RIG_REPO_ACME_CRAN_USERNAME=alice
   export RIG_REPO_ACME_CRAN_PASSWORD=secret
   ```

   The name of a repository is the name you gave to `rig repos add`, the
   name in `--with-repos <name>=<url>`, or the `name` of the
   `[[repository]]` entry in `rproj.toml`. A URL in `--with-repos` without
   a name is named after its host, e.g. `cran.acme.com`, so its variables
   are `RIG_REPO_CRAN_ACME_COM_USERNAME` and
   `RIG_REPO_CRAN_ACME_COM_PASSWORD`. The `name` column of
   [`rig auth status`](reference/auth.qmd#rig-auth-status) shows the name
   of each repository. These variables do not apply to the repositories
   built into rig with their own metadata: CRAN, Bioconductor and P3M.

   If `_USERNAME` is not set, rig uses the username in the URL. This works
   well on CI systems, where secrets are usually environment variables.
3. **A PPM SSO token**, see [below](#posit-package-manager-sso).
4. **A netrc file.** rig reads the file in `PKG_NETRC_PATH` or `NETRC`, or
   `~/.netrc` (on Windows also `~/_netrc`). A netrc file has one entry for
   each host:

   ```
   machine cran.acme.com login alice password secret
   ```

   If the URL has a username, rig only uses an entry with the same `login`.
   rig only uses the `default` entry for URLs that have a username. Make
   sure that only you can read the file: `chmod 600 ~/.netrc`.
5. **The system credential store**: the macOS Keychain, the Windows
   Credential Manager, or a Secret Service on Linux (e.g. GNOME Keyring or
   KWallet). rig only looks here for URLs that include a username. The
   easiest way to save a password here is
   [`rig auth login`](reference/auth.qmd#rig-auth-login):

   ```sh
   rig auth login https://cran.acme.com/cran --username alice
   ```

   rig asks for the password. On a CI system, use `--password -` to read it
   from the standard input instead. You can also give the name of a
   repository instead of its URL. For a repository added as
   `rig repos add acme https://alice@cran.acme.com/cran`, this is enough:

   ```sh
   rig auth login acme
   ```

   You can save the password before you add the repository. If no
   configured repository uses it yet, rig tells you.

   The entries are keyed the same way as in pak and the keyring R package,
   so you can also use `keyring::key_set()` in R. rig tries these keys, for
   the user in the URL, and uses the first one that exists:

   ```
   https://alice@cran.acme.com/cran
   https://cran.acme.com/cran
   https://alice@cran.acme.com
   https://cran.acme.com
   cran.acme.com
   ```

   The repository URL in these keys does not have the `/src/contrib` or
   `/bin/...` part, or a `/__linux__/<distro>` part, so all files of a
   repository use the same key.

   Linux servers often have no Secret Service running. rig then skips this
   step, so use a netrc file or environment variables there.

## Posit Package Manager SSO

If your PPM instance uses single sign-on (SSO), log in with your browser:

```sh
export PACKAGEMANAGER_ADDRESS=https://ppm.acme.com
rig auth login
```

rig prints a URL and a code, and opens the URL in your browser. Once you log
in there, rig saves the PPM token in `~/.ppm/tokens.toml`. This is the same
file pak uses, so after you log in with rig, pak can use the token as well,
and the other way around.

If the host name matches `PACKAGEMANAGER_ADDRESS` then you do not need a
username in the PPM repository URL. If you still want one, like for pak,
use `__token__`: `https://__token__@ppm.acme.com/cran/latest`.

rig does not open a browser by itself during other commands. When the token
expires, log in again with `rig auth login`.

On a CI system that has an OIDC identity token, put the identity token into
a file, and set `PACKAGEMANAGER_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` to its path. rig then
exchanges it for a PPM token itself, without a browser.

## Checking your setup

[`rig auth status`](reference/auth.qmd#rig-auth-status) shows which
repositories of the default R installation (and which repositories added
with `rig repos add`) have credentials, and where they come from. It also
lists the saved PPM SSO tokens and when they expire. It never prints the
passwords or tokens.

```sh
rig auth status
rig auth status https://alice@cran.acme.com/cran
```

If a download fails with HTTP status 401 or 403, rig's error message
suggests running `rig auth status`.

To use the same credentials outside of rig, e.g. with `curl`,
[`rig auth token`](reference/auth.qmd#rig-auth-token) prints the password or
token rig would send to a URL.

To remove saved credentials, use
[`rig auth logout`](reference/auth.qmd#rig-auth-logout).
